messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing a weird p95/p99 jump on shared-gpu pool-b around 06:12 UTC, throughput steady but tails up from ~45ms -> ~220ms. correlates with a single tenant spike on mem-bandwidth graphs. cc @cheng @dave
cheng: digging into perf dashboards now, grabbing nsys traces for the top offending host (b-gpu-17)
dave: which tenant id? can we throttle at the router level first?
maria: tenant `tenant-phi-42` — they had a burst of long context fp32 requests. tried a quick concurrency cap (2) at 06:25 and p99 dropped to ~80ms for ~10min then drifted back up
emily: pasted nsys summary from b-gpu-17: ```
== Summary ==
GPU Memory BW: 720 GB/s peak
DRAM Utilization: 92% during spike
Kernel: attention_fp32_unfused_v1 dominant (72% of global memory ops)
KV cache writes: 13% of mem traffic
```
cheng: that kernel is the unfused FP32 attention path — it bypasses some locality optimizations. ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ looks like one tenant's workload is pulling full-precision long sequences; combined with concurrent tenants causes DRAM to saturate
maria: also saw KV cache churn: per-tenant KV slot misses went from 2% -> 27% during the spike, suggests eviction pressure from the same tenant's long sequences
dave: can we force-serve that tenant on a different kernel variant (quantized or fused) without a full deploy? maybe runtime can route to kernel-optimized shim
cheng: we tried runtime kernel override in staging. patch: `KERNEL_PREFERENCE=force:fused_q8` — it reduced mem BW to ~320 GB/s locally. But model quality for that tenant is slightly off; need to check evals
emily: quick experiment notes: 1) concurrency cap -> immediate tail improvement 2) kernel override -> sustainable mem reduction but +0.6% perplexity on eval set 3) KV pinning (increase per-tenant KV slots) -> reduced misses but increases memory footprint
maria: options on the table: throttle concurrency (easy, perf), route tenant to dedicated node pool (costly), force kernel override (risk of quality regression), or increase KV reservation for tenant (memory tradeoff)
dave: short term: apply concurrency cap (2) and increase KV reservation for tenant-phi-42 by +20 slots. who wants to own?
cheng: I can apply the cap and KV bump in the next 10m and monitor. will also push a transient kernel-override for canary 1 replica to validate quality impact
emily: I'll run the eval harness against the canary traffic set and report delta by EOD
infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: canary applied to b-gpu-17 (replica id r-3398) at 06:48 UTC
maria: after the cap + KV bump p99 dropped to ~65ms and mem BW to ~410 GB/s for 30m, but we still see periodics at ~100ms during times of cluster-wide batch peaks
cheng: hypothesis: batching heuristic combined with that tenant's request length creates super-batches that overflow the fused kernel's working set, causing fallback to unfused kernel under certain seq_len combos. gathering batching traces (`/var/log/runtime/batch-traces/`) now
dave: longer-term: add per-tenant mem-bandwidth telemetry and a soft admission controller that prevents super-batches crossing a mem-bandwidth threshold. Could also add kernel-selection rule: prefer fused_q8 for tenants with >X requests/sec of long context
emaria: agree. immediate action items: [cheng] implement cap + KV bump (in-progress), [emily] eval canary, [dave] spec admission controller prototype. We'll reconvene in #eng-runtime in 2 hours or earlier if tails reappear :thumbsup:
cheng: noted — will post logs and a concise postmortem if this recurs after changes
emily: posted quick eval: quality delta +0.4% on canary, acceptable per SLO. recommending keep kernel override for that shard for next 24h while we design admission controller
maria: thanks team. adding documentation task: how to detect mem-bandwidth noisy-neighbor vs kernel quality trade-offs (for on-call runbook)
infra-bot: incident-tracker created: INC-2026-memory-bandwidth-noisy-tenant, priority P2
_meta: generated for dataset: slack eng-runtime noisy-neighbor memory bandwidth investigation
